data.name: The Last Cargo
data.detailed_description:
OUR NEXT GAMES:


Acerca do jogo

The Last Cargo is a atmospheric top-down survival horror that invoking the need of deeper reflection. The action takes place in a mysterious building with specific features, where many objects of your surroundings are randomized during each play.




The situation of our character is unique. His beliefs, imposed onto him, have limited his movement in the form of a wheelchair. To survive you must explore floor after floor looking for food, ammunition and many other helpful items.

The main theme of The Last Cargo is indoctrination, whose purpose is to control the way an individual perceives and evaluates reality. Your goal is to recover autonomy and subjectivity for the eponymous cargo.



  • Every game is different due to unique randomizing system
  • Consequences and Variables mechanics influencing many additional factors in the game
  • 18 perks (adaptations) each with 3 stages of development
  • 6 different endings dependent on the player's choices
  • 3 difficulty levels and optional permadeath mode
  • It's not an easy game (draw conclusions and learn from mistakes)

reviews.review:
An experience that feels very much like a budget minigame which could be found and played as a novelty inside a much larger game. Although clear efforts were made to give the game some degree of substance it's simply just not engaging.


The main gameplay formula involves players navigating through a somewhat bare randomly generated environment performing rudimentary fetch quests, while also occasionally interacting with objects to scavenge for crafting resources. Players search around the environment for a computer terminal which then gives them an MMO-esque fetch quest such as find X amount of thing, find X thing and take it to X place; then afterwards players must go back to the terminal before returning to the elevator of said floor. There is little depth to the gameplay beyond that, and what additional mechanics exist in the game are superficial. 

There are basic enemies wandering around the floor but all they do is gravitate towards the player, then explode; which is mostly just a nuisance easily countered by baiting out the explosion. There is also a special, unstoppable enemy following the player around; which is also mostly just a nuisance as they are avoided simply by... moving away from them. Players have a stun ability which does help to add a bit of interactivity to the experience, but the player's gun is seldom needed and often better used for safely breaking glass walls. There is also a stealth element where players can move slower to become quieter, but it's unclear why this would ever be needed as I encountered no threats that merited stealth.

Players can acquire items that provide light, yet the environments are often decently lit enough so that extra light isn't really needed. Players can also acquire ammunition for their weapon which mostly amounts to shooting walls to open them up. There are resources associated with healing and stamina but really all these resources and items do little to diversify the actual gameplay; which is navigating around a basic interior doing fetch quests while occasionally avoiding a big stalker enemy and smaller exploding enemies.

It's just not engaging to play. There's not really any combat, as enemies are almost exclusively defeated by simply avoiding them. There's not really any stealth, as there's just no point when enemies are so easily avoided. The objectives are basic, repetitive fetch quests. There's a resource management system, but it's not impactful enough to make up for all the aforementioned lackluster elements. Every level generally looks the same and has little in the environment besides resource nodes, there's only two kinds of regularly encountered enemies, the game does introduce level modifiers but they're also fairly simple. 


The game looks nice, sounds fine, it has an interesting although very awkwardly translated story; but it's just not engaging. Running around a mostly empty environment doing fetch quests while easily avoiding two types of very basic threats then sometimes having to stop for resource management is the experience. The core gameplay loop is simply boring and underdeveloped.

If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38950844-Anoemalous/] here [/url].


[i]This is a revised version of my previous review, having revisited the game on the developer's request after the game received a new update. However aside from the movement controls being improved it seems that many of my original criticisms are still applicable. Yet in direct conversation the developers attempted to dismiss all of my criticism as the result of me having the wrong "expectations" for the game.

Thus I do not recommend this game as I find it neither engaging nor enjoyable. And I especially do not recommend it now after the developers, who explicitly asked me to revisit the game, brazenly dismissed all of my criticism under the false and baseless accusation that I only dislike this game because I have the wrong "expectations" of it. Yes, to an extent, that is true; I dislike this game because I expected it to actually be engaging and enjoyable. Which apparently by their own admission is not the developer's target demographic.

It seems the developer is attempting to misrepresent our conversation in their response below, so now I'm editing this again. Basically what happened was they asked me to play the game again, I played the game again and gave them feedback afterwards; then their immediate response was to imply that I dislike this game because I have the wrong expectations. Now they're lying about it and trying to claim that actually they never dismissed my criticism and were simply disagreeing with me; even though their literal only response to my criticism was just them suggesting that my judgement is unsound because of my expectations. Which is them dismissing my criticism, with the notion that I'm too stupid to rate a video game constructively. They did not even provide an argument to support their accusation of expectations either, it was purely an ad hominem.

They're also claiming that most of the basic changes I recommended such as adding more enemies, biomes or making the game less repetitive have no place in their game and would disrupt the "message". Well if the message of their game is boredom then I must agree, adding more variety and engagement would certainly disrupt that. So again they're technically correct, if they literally want this game to be repetitive and boring then I did indeed have the wrong expectations of it when I submitted that feedback. 

As a developer myself the argument that basic game elements like enemy variety are a "vague idea" that would "disrupt" some "message" in the game is beyond nonsensical; and a ridiculous way to disregard simple feedback.[/i]
reviews.developer_response:
I just now saw what you write at the end of the review - and wow. You exaggerating our private conversation SO much to make it seem like we are bad developers that are not listening to players criticism. It's not nice to lie like that.

I never dismissed your or anyone criticism, quite the opposite. Most of the flaws you talk about (in your old review) have been corrected. That's why I asked you if you have time to check new update. We still have a whole list of changes that we are slowly working on - so any constructive criticism is always good. If we didn't take criticism/opinions about the game seriously, we wouldn't releasing updates and patches ;)

You also claim that "Yet in direct conversation the developers attempted to dismiss all of my criticism as the result of me having the wrong expectations for the game" - which is untrue. I was telling you that I don't fully agree with your new review (regarding update 1.3), but you have the right to criticize - for which then I thanked you. I never dismissed your criticism.

I said that maybe you expecting the game to be something it's not - ONLY when in private messages you told us what you think we should add to the game (more enemies, more "biomes", be less "repetitive" etc.) - and that's great "vague" ideas! But most of them have no place in our game, otherwise they will disrupt the overall message. So if this offended you, then I truly don't know how or why.
